name: Jasper National Park
description: A UNESCO Dark Sky Preserve — one of the darkest, largest protected dark sky areas in the world. Mountain-framed horizons and zero light pollution make every aurora unforgettable.

name: Elk Island National Park
description: Only 35 km east of Edmonton, this dark sky preserve is the most accessible spot in Alberta for aurora chasers who need a quick escape from the city.

name: Abraham Lake
description: A reservoir along the North Saskatchewan River famous for its bubbling ice in winter and stunning wide-open skies. Reflections on the water double the aurora spectacle.

name: Kananaskis Country
description: A vast wilderness southwest of Calgary with minimal light pollution and dramatic mountain silhouettes. Multiple viewpoints and camping areas give photographers great options.

name: Writing-on-Stone Provincial Park
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site near the US border. The Milk River valley's hoodoos create a surreal foreground for southern Alberta aurora displays.

name: Banff National Park
description: Canada's first national park combines world-class dark skies with iconic mountain scenery. Lake Minnewanka and the Bow Valley Parkway are prime viewing corridors.

name: Cypress Hills Interprovincial Park
description: Sitting above the surrounding plains at over 1,400 m, Cypress Hills offers some of the darkest skies in southeastern Alberta with a 360° horizon away from any city glow.
